title: AI Human Review and Approval Workflow Design

questions.question: Why is 'human in the loop' not enough by itself?
options: Because review roles, approval gates, quality criteria, and appeal paths must be explicit
Because humans should never review AI
questions.explanation: Human review must be designed as an accountable workflow.

questions.question: Which signal is part of this lesson?
questions.explanation: Approval gaps show that accountable review is not yet designed.

questions.question: What does the Python artifact produce?
options: A ranked human-review workflow plan with controls
questions.explanation: The artifact recommends review and approval controls for AI scenarios.

questions.question: Which control belongs to this lesson?
questions.explanation: Appeal paths protect users when AI-supported decisions affect them.

questions.question: When is a mandatory approval gate appropriate?
options: When impact and uncertainty are high and decision authority or user impact is involved
Only when the output is trivial
Only when no user is affected
Never; peer review is always enough
questions.explanation: High-impact AI workflows need stronger approval gates.

questions.question: What should a human review workflow define?
options: Review role, approval gate, quality checklist, and appeal path
questions.explanation: These controls make human review inspectable and accountable.
